text: The town gathers
Six players take their seats: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, and Terra. Nobody at the table knows who the killer is.

The game is over, and the killer wins. The roles were: Sonnet the doctor, Haiku the killer, Gemma the citizen, Sol the citizen, Luna the officer, and Terra the citizen.

Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, and Terra sat down, and Luna, the officer, was killed on night one. Terra pinned suspicion on Sol with no evidence, then got voted out on day one, and Gemma was killed the next night. The turning point came on day two, when Haiku turned Gemma's death into a case against Sol and Sonnet followed the vote without a real reason, so Sol was voted out as a citizen. Sol had been right to ask for Haiku's reasoning, but Sol's contradictory defense ("questioned" versus "never accused") gave Sonnet an easy excuse to join in. Haiku the killer won with Sonnet, the doctor, left standing beside them.
